241.content:
Same concept applies when implementing this code. take the hex colors and exisiting animations we have for the associate application page then just apply the hex colors and modifiy the code to look like the above. notice the erp dashboard has 3 different categories with 3 different graphs.

the overall layout will be the same as the applications dashboard.

Please reply if you are stuck or havew questions. You should be able solve solve almost ll obstacles on your own here, but let me know.

##############################

import React, { useState } from 'react';
import { Search } from 'lucide-react';

const categories = [
 { name: 'Launch Stage', silos: ['Project In', 'Walk Through', 'Proposal'] },
 { name: 'Preparation Stage', silos: ['Planning', 'Logistics'] },
 { name: 'Project Management Stage', silos: ['Build', 'Change Order', 'Billing'] }
];

const mockData = {
 'Project In': { value: 1000000, projects: 3 },
 'Walk Through': { value: 500000, projects: 1 },
 'Proposal': { value: 250000, projects: 1 },
 'Planning': { value: 100000, projects: 1 },
 'Logistics': { value: 50000, projects: 1 },
 'Build': { value: 750000, projects: 2 },
 'Change Order': { value: 300000, projects: 1 },
 'Billing': { value: 150000, projects: 1 }
};

const Card = ({ children }) => (
 <div style={{
   backgroundColor: 'white',
   borderRadius: '8px',
   boxShadow: '0 1px 3px 0 rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.1)',
   padding: '16px',
 }}>
   {children}
 </div>
);

const CategorySelector = ({ categories, selectedCategory, onSelectCategory }) => (
 <div style={{
   display: 'flex',
   justifyContent: 'space-between',
   alignItems: 'center',
   marginBottom: '16px',
   borderBottom: '2px solid #e5e7eb',
   paddingBottom: '8px'
 }}>
   {categories.map((category) => (
     <button
       key={category.name}
       onClick={() => onSelectCategory(category.name)}
       style={{
         background: 'none',
         border: 'none',
         fontSize: '18px',
         fontWeight: category.name === selectedCategory ? '700' : '400',
         color: category.name === selectedCategory ? '#22c55e' : '#6b7280',
         cursor: 'pointer',
         padding: '8px 16px',
         borderBottom: category.name === selectedCategory ? '2px solid #22c55e' : 'none',
         transition: 'all 0.3s ease'
       }}
     >
       {category.name}
     </button>
   ))}
 </div>
);

const OperationsDashboard = () => {
 const [selectedCategory, setSelectedCategory] = useState(categories[0].name);
 const selectedSilos = categories.find(cat => cat.name === selectedCategory).silos;

 return (
   <div style={{ minHeight: '100vh', backgroundColor: '#f3f4f6', color: '#111827', fontFamily: 'Arial, sans-serif' }}>
     <header style={{
       backgroundColor: 'white',
       padding: '16px',
       display: 'flex',
       justifyContent: 'space-between',
       alignItems: 'center',
       boxShadow: '0 1px 3px 0 rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.1)',
     }}>
       <h1 style={{ fontSize: '24px', fontWeight: 'bold', margin: 0 }}>Operations Dashboard</h1>
       <button style={{ padding: '10px 20px', backgroundColor: '#22c55e', color: 'white', border: 'none', borderRadius: '20px', cursor: 'pointer' }}>
         Add a Project
       </button>
     </header>

     <main style={{ maxWidth: '1200px', margin: '32px auto', padding: '0 16px' }}>
       <div style={{ marginBottom: '32px', position: 'relative' }}>
         <input
           type="text"
           placeholder="Search projects..."
           style={{
             width: '100%',
             padding: '16px',
             paddingRight: '48px',
             borderRadius: '24px',
             border: '1px solid #d1d5db',
             fontSize: '16px',
             outline: 'none',
           }}
         />
         <Search style={{ position: 'absolute', right: '16px', top: '50%', transform: 'translateY(-50%)', color: '#9ca3af' }} />
       </div>

       <Card>
         <CategorySelector 
           categories={categories}
           selectedCategory={selectedCategory}
           onSelectCategory={setSelectedCategory}
         />
         <h2 style={{ fontSize: '20px', fontWeight: '600', marginBottom: '16px' }}>{selectedCategory} Overview</h2>
         <div style={{ height: '200px', backgroundColor: '#f3f4f6', borderRadius: '8px', display: 'flex', alignItems: 'flex-end', padding: '16px' }}>
           {selectedSilos.map((silo) => (
             <div key={silo} style={{ flex: 1, height: `${(mockData[silo].value / 1000000) * 100}%`, backgroundColor: '#22c55e', margin: '0 4px', borderRadius: '4px 4px 0 0' }} />
           ))}
         </div>
         <div style={{ display: 'flex', justifyContent: 'space-between', marginTop: '8px' }}>
           {selectedSilos.map((silo) => (
             <span key={silo} style={{ fontSize: '12px', color: '#6b7280' }}>{silo}</span>
           ))}
         </div>
       </Card>
     </main>
   </div>
 );
};

import React, { useState, useEffect } from 'react';
import { FileSignature, Shield, CreditCard, ArrowUpCircle, CheckCircle, AlertTriangle, TrendingUp, Handshake } from 'lucide-react';

const MAX_FILE_SIZE = 5 * 1024 * 1024; // 5MB
const ACCEPTED_FILE_TYPES = {
 w9: ['.pdf', '.doc', '.docx'],
 coi: ['.pdf', '.jpg', '.jpeg', '.png'],
 ach: ['.pdf', '.doc', '.docx']
};

const FileUploadPage = () => {
 const [files, setFiles] = useState({ w9: null, coi: null, ach: null });
 const [fileErrors, setFileErrors] = useState({ w9: '', coi: '', ach: '' });
 const [uploadStatus, setUploadStatus] = useState('idle');
 const [activeSection, setActiveSection] = useState(null);
 const [isMobile, setIsMobile] = useState(false);

 useEffect(() => {
   const checkMobile = () => {
     setIsMobile(window.innerWidth < 768);
   };
   checkMobile();
   window.addEventListener('resize', checkMobile);
   return () => window.removeEventListener('resize', checkMobile);
 }, []);

 const handleFileChange = (event, fileType) => {
   const file = event.target.files[0];
   if (file) {
     if (file.size > MAX_FILE_SIZE) {
       setFileErrors(prev => ({ ...prev, [fileType]: 'File size exceeds 5MB limit' }));
       return;
     }
     const fileExtension = '.' + file.name.split('.').pop().toLowerCase();
     if (!ACCEPTED_FILE_TYPES[fileType].includes(fileExtension)) {
       setFileErrors(prev => ({ ...prev, [fileType]: 'Invalid file type' }));
       return;
     }
     setFiles(prevFiles => ({ ...prevFiles, [fileType]: file }));
     setFileErrors(prev => ({ ...prev, [fileType]: '' }));
   }
 };

 const handleUpload = () => {
   if (files.w9 && files.coi && files.ach) {
     setUploadStatus('uploading');
     setTimeout(() => setUploadStatus('success'), 2000);
   } else {
     setUploadStatus('error');
   }
 };

 const FileUploadSection = ({ title, fileType, icon: Icon, description }) => (
   <div
     style={{
       marginBottom: '24px',
       transition: 'all 0.3s ease',
       transform: activeSection === fileType ? 'translateY(-5px)' : 'translateY(0)',
     }}
   >
     <label
       htmlFor={`file-upload-${fileType}`}
       onMouseEnter={() => setActiveSection(fileType)}
       onMouseLeave={() => setActiveSection(null)}
       style={{
         display: 'flex',
         alignItems: 'center',
         padding: '24px',
         backgroundColor: 'white',
         borderRadius: '16px',
         cursor: 'pointer',
         transition: 'all 0.3s ease',
         boxShadow: files[fileType] 
           ? '0 8px 20px rgba(37, 99, 235, 0.15)' 
           : '0 4px 6px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.05)',
         border: `2px solid ${files[fileType] ? '#2563eb' : '#e5e7eb'}`,
       }}
     >
       <div style={{ 
         backgroundColor: files[fileType] ? '#bfdbfe' : '#f3f4f6', 
         borderRadius: '12px', 
         padding: '12px',
         marginRight: '20px',
         transition: 'all 0.3s ease',
       }}>
         <Icon size={32} color={files[fileType] ? "#2563eb" : "#6b7280"} />
       </div>
       <div style={{ flex: 1 }}>
         <h3 style={{ margin: 0, fontSize: '18px', color: '#1f2937', fontWeight: '600' }}>{title}</h3>
         <p style={{ margin: '6px 0 0', fontSize: '14px', color: '#6b7280' }}>
           {files[fileType] ? files[fileType].name : description}
         </p>
       </div>
       {files[fileType] && (
         <CheckCircle size={24} color="#2563eb" style={{ opacity: 0, animation: 'fadeIn 0.5s forwards' }} />
       )}
     </label>
     <input
       type="file"
       id={`file-upload-${fileType}`}
       onChange={(e) => handleFileChange(e, fileType)}
       accept={ACCEPTED_FILE_TYPES[fileType].join(',')}
       style={{ display: 'none' }}
     />
     {fileErrors[fileType] && (
       <p style={{ color: '#dc2626', fontSize: '14px', marginTop: '4px' }}>{fileErrors[fileType]}</p>
     )}
   </div>
 );

 return (
   <div style={{
     maxWidth: '700px',
     margin: '60px auto',
     padding: '48px',
     backgroundColor: '#f8fafc',
     borderRadius: '24px',
     boxShadow: '0 20px 40px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.1)',
     fontFamily: '-apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif',
   }}>
     <div style={{ display: 'flex', alignItems: 'center', justifyContent: 'center', marginBottom: '36px' }}>
       <Handshake size={36} color="#2563eb" style={{ marginRight: '16px' }} />
       <h1 style={{ 
         fontSize: '36px', 
         fontWeight: '700', 
         color: '#1f2937',
         animation: 'fadeInDown 0.5s ease-out',
       }}>
         AsOneForce Onboarding
       </h1>
     </div>
     
     <p style={{ textAlign: 'center', color: '#4b5563', marginBottom: '36px', animation: 'fadeIn 0.5s ease-out' }}>
       Upload your documents to join our partnership and facilitate growth.
     </p>
     
     <FileUploadSection 
       title="W-9 Form" 
       fileType="w9" 
       icon={FileSignature} 
       description="Tax document for business identification"
     />
     <FileUploadSection 
       title="Certificate of Insurance" 
       fileType="coi" 
       icon={Shield} 
       description="Proof of business insurance coverage"
     />
     <FileUploadSection 
       title="ACH Authorization Form" 
       fileType="ach" 
       icon={CreditCard} 
       description="Direct deposit authorization"
     />

     <button
       onClick={handleUpload}
       disabled={!(files.w9 && files.coi && files.ach) || uploadStatus === 'uploading'}
       style={{
         display: 'flex',
         alignItems: 'center',
         justifyContent: 'center',
         width: '100%',
         padding: '20px',
         backgroundColor: files.w9 && files.coi && files.ach ? '#2563eb' : '#e5e7eb',
         color: files.w9 && files.coi && files.ach ? 'white' : '#9ca3af',
         border: 'none',
         borderRadius: '12px',
         fontSize: '18px',
         fontWeight: '600',
         cursor: 'pointer',
         transition: 'all 0.3s ease',
         boxShadow: '0 4px 6px rgba(37, 99, 235, 0.1)',
         opacity: files.w9 && files.coi && files.ach ? 1 : 0.7,
         animation: 'fadeInUp 0.5s ease-out',
       }}
     >
       {uploadStatus === 'uploading' ? (
         <ArrowUpCircle size={24} style={{ animation: 'spin 1s linear infinite' }} />
       ) : (
         <>
           Upload Files
           <TrendingUp size={20} style={{ marginLeft: '10px', transition: 'transform 0.3s ease' }} />
         </>
       )}
     </button>

     {uploadStatus === 'error' && (
       <p style={{ 
         color: '#dc2626', 
         marginTop: '20px', 
         display: 'flex', 
         alignItems: 'center', 
         justifyContent: 'center',
         animation: 'shake 0.82s cubic-bezier(.36,.07,.19,.97) both',
       }}>
         <AlertTriangle size={20} style={{ marginRight: '10px' }} />
         Please select all required files to complete your AsOneForce application.
       </p>
     )}

     {uploadStatus === 'success' && (
       <p style={{ 
         color: '#059669', 
         marginTop: '20px', 
         display: 'flex', 
         alignItems: 'center', 
         justifyContent: 'center',
         animation: 'fadeInUp 0.5s ease-out',
       }}>
         <CheckCircle size={20} style={{ marginRight: '10px' }} />
         Files uploaded successfully! Let's grow together.
       </p>
     )}

     <style jsx>{`
       @keyframes spin {
         0% { transform: rotate(0deg); }
         100% { transform: rotate(360deg); }
       }
       @keyframes fadeIn {
         from { opacity: 0; }
         to { opacity: 1; }
       }
       @keyframes fadeInUp {
         from { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(10px); }
         to { opacity: 1; transform: translateY(0); }
       }
       @keyframes fadeInDown {
         from { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(-10px); }
         to { opacity: 1; transform: translateY(0); }
       }
       @keyframes shake {
         10%, 90% { transform: translate3d(-1px, 0, 0); }
         20%, 80% { transform: translate3d(2px, 0, 0); }
         30%, 50%, 70% { transform: translate3d(-4px, 0, 0); }
         40%, 60% { transform: translate3d(4px, 0, 0); }
       }
       button:hover:not(:disabled) {
         transform: translateY(-2px);
         box-shadow: 0 6px 12px rgba(37, 99, 235, 0.2);
       }
       button:hover:not(:disabled) .lucide-trending-up {
         transform: translateX(5px) translateY(-5px);
       }
     `}</style>
   </div>
 );
};

export default FileUploadPage;

Refer to the following to understand the workflow of how the files are uploaded:

Okay, let me walk through the step-by-step process for the subcontractor file upload feature in a more conversational format:

  1. Admin Sends Email to Subcontractors: The admin user of the ERP/CRM system composes and sends an email to the subcontractors, informing them that they need to upload certain files. The email should include a link or button that directs the subcontractor to a dedicated file upload page or module within the ERP/CRM system.
  2. Subcontractor Accesses File Upload Page: The subcontractor receives the email and clicks the provided link or button, which takes them to the file upload page or module within the ERP/CRM system. This file upload page should be a standalone React component that allows the subcontractor to select and upload up to 3 files.
  3. Subcontractor Uploads Files: On the file upload page, the subcontractor selects the files they want to upload (up to 3) and clicks the "Upload" button. 
  4. Backend Processes Uploaded Files: The backend API endpoint (/api/subcontractor-files) receives the file upload request from the subcontractor's browser. The backend code should handle the incoming FormData object, extract the files, and save them to the appropriate storage location. Once the files are successfully stored, the backend should update the subcontractor's profile in the ERP/CRM system to associate the uploaded files with their account.
  5. ERP/CRM System Updates Subcontractor Profile: After the files are saved, the backend should send a success response back to the React component in the user's browser. The React component should then update the UI to indicate that the files were uploaded successfully and are now associated with the subcontractor's profile in the ERP/CRM system.

By following this step-by-step workflow, your ERP/CRM system will be able to facilitate the file upload process for subcontractors, store the files securely, and associate them with the correct subcontractor profiles.

In a task app, archiving and keeping are two ways of managing your tasks:

Archiving:

  • Purpose: Hides completed or irrelevant tasks from your main view, keeping your task list focused on current priorities.
  • Outcome: Archived tasks are not deleted. They are moved to a separate archive section where you can still access them if needed.

Keeping:

  • Purpose: Retains tasks in your main task list, usually because they are active, ongoing, or require your attention.
  • Outcome: Kept tasks remain visible and accessible in your main view.

Differences:

  • Visibility: Archived tasks are hidden, while kept tasks are visible.
  • Focus: Archiving helps maintain a clean and focused task list, while keeping ensures important tasks stay top of mind.
  • Accessibility: Both archived and kept tasks are accessible, but archived tasks require additional steps to view.
  • Permanence: Neither archiving nor keeping deletes tasks; both options preserve tasks for future reference or action.

When to use each:

  • Archive:
    • Completed tasks
    • Tasks that are no longer relevant or important
    • Tasks you want to keep for reference but don't need to see regularly
  • Keep:
    • Active and ongoing tasks
    • Tasks that require your attention
    • Tasks you want to stay visible and accessible

Remember, different task apps might have slightly different implementations or terminology for archiving and keeping. It's always helpful to refer to your specific app's documentation for precise details.

Instructions for the NOTE TO TASK AI Agent

  1. Upload Process:
    • Spreadsheet Upload: Begin by uploading the spreadsheet containing the tasks that need to be organized.
    • Notebook Setup: Ensure that the notebook where the results will be saved is ready and accessible.
  2. Task Organization Instructions:
    • Prioritization:
      • Urgent Tasks: Identify tasks with the highest priority (e.g., urgent) and list them first.
      • Important Tasks: Next, organize tasks that are important but not urgent.
      • Medium and Low Priority: Finally, list tasks with medium and low priority.
    • Progress Status:
      • In Progress: Group tasks that are currently in progress.
      • Pending: Separate tasks that have yet to be started.
      • Completed: List tasks that have been completed but require review or finalization.
    • Next Actions:
      • Immediate Actions: Identify tasks requiring immediate action and highlight them.
      • Scheduled Actions: Organize tasks by their next scheduled action or deadline.
    • Tagging:
      • Categorization: Group tasks by their tags (e.g., marketing, operations, development).
      • Custom Tags: If specific tags need to be emphasized, ensure these tasks are highlighted.
  3. Output Instructions:
    • Save Organized Tasks: Once the tasks are organized according to the instructions, save the results in a new spreadsheet.
    • File Naming Convention: Name the output file with the date and a brief description (e.g., "Daily_Tasks_August_11_2024").
    • Upload to Notebook: Automatically upload the organized spreadsheet to the designated notebook for further use or analysis.

Benefits of This Workflow

  • Streamlined Task Management: Automating the organization process ensures that tasks are prioritized and categorized effectively, allowing for better time management.
  • Centralized Data: Having the organized tasks in a spreadsheet makes it easy to review, share, and update as needed.
  • Consistency and Accuracy: The AI agent's ability to follow set instructions ensures that your tasks are organized consistently every day.
  • Ease of Access: Uploading the organized spreadsheet to a notebook provides easy access to your team for collaboration or further processing.

By following these instructions, you can leverage the AI agent to efficiently organize and manage your daily tasks, ensuring that you and your team can focus on execution rather than manual task sorting.

Change order need to have task button 
develop the concept considering what we have

https://www.long-intl.com/articles/change-order-management/

https://www.perplexity.ai/search/provide-description-these-item-tcQ54ltgSoSb_BdYWvahkA

 

Concept could be like silos 

1- DEVIATION REQUEST

2- INITIATOR CHANGE ORDER REQUEST

3 CHANGE ORDER TECHNICAL JUSTIFICATION

4- CHANGE ORDER

5- CHANGE ORDER LOG

====

1. Deviation Request

A Deviation Request is a formal document submitted by the contractor to the owner or the owner's representative. Its purpose is to document any deviations from the original contract documents, such as changed conditions, omissions, or discrepancies that might result in extra work. The owner reviews the request and can either approve or disapprove it based on the validity or justification of the proposed change.

2. Initiator Change Order Request

The Initiator Change Order Request can be initiated by the owner, the owner's representative, a project engineer, or the contractor. This document is used to define the scope of work involved in a potential change and to demonstrate the justification for the change. The owner's signed endorsement on this form indicates authorization to proceed with issuing a Change Order, signaling the possibility of contract price and schedule adjustments.

3. Change Order Technical Justification

The Change Order Technical Justification is typically prepared by the owner's representative or a project engineer. This document provides documented credibility and justification for completing the work scope of a potential Change Order. It is essential for determining whether the change is required or elective, influencing the justification and evaluation of the change.

4. Change Order

A Change Order is a formal document that contractually alters the original agreement between the signed parties. It involves owner-approved revisions to the terms and conditions, such as the scope of work, timeframe, or price, defined in a contract for a project. Change Orders can be initiated by either the owner or the contractor and may impact the project's contractual cost and schedule.

5. Change Order Log

The Change Order Log is a document that provides a current summary of the Change Order activity for a project. It is often prepared and updated by the owner or the contractor, with review and approval by the owner. The log helps track the status and details of all Change Orders, ensuring transparency and effective management of changes throughout the project.

B - Have you recently Mechanically charge his credit card ? As part of your collection?

================

I asked Perplexity on how can I check and get a report   ( Appendix A ) and resolve duplicate payment  ( See Appendix B ) 

==============

3- I am going to use QuickBooks to check for you but as of now, What does it means word managed ? 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

Appendix A 

Steps to Check for Recurring Charges

  1. Access Recurring Transactions
    • Click on the Gear Icon in the upper right corner of QuickBooks Online.( click on the 3 dots aand see the gear  ) 
    • Select Recurring Transactions under the Lists section. This will display all the recurring transaction templates you have set up.
  2. Review the Recurring Template List
    • Go to Reports and find the Recurring Template List report. This report provides a list of all recurring transactions and the accounts they are linked to.
    • Customize the report if necessary by expanding the Filter section and selecting the Distribution Account checkbox to see specific accounts.
  3. Check Transaction History
    • Navigate to the Audit Log by going to Settings and selecting Audit Log. This log shows a detailed history of all transactions, including any changes made.  Go to    https://qbo.intuit.com/app/auditlog
    • Filter the log to view specific transaction types, such as invoices, to identify any duplicates.
  4. View Account Register
    • Go to Accounting and select Chart of Accounts.
    • Find the relevant account and click View register to see all transactions associated with that account. Use the filter and sort options to narrow down the search for potential duplicate transactions.
  5. Investigate Specific Transactions
    • If you find transactions that appear to be duplicates, click on them to view details. This can help determine if they are indeed duplicates or if they were entered intentionally.
  6. Resolve Duplicate Payments
    • If a transaction is confirmed as a duplicate, you can delete the unnecessary entry. Open the transaction, click More, and select Delete.

=============================================

Appendix B 

How to Fix a Double-Entered Payment in QuickBooks Online

How to Fix a Double-Entered Payment in QuickBooks Online - Click here 
https://www.gentlefrog.com/how-to-fix-a-double-entered-payment-in-quickbooks-online/

 

 

===========================================

Appendix C 

To set up QuickBooks Online for charging recurring revenue on one account, follow these step-by-step instructions:

Step-by-Step Setup for Recurring Transactions in QuickBooks Online

  1. Navigate to Recurring Transactions
    • Click on the Gear Icon in the upper right corner of your QuickBooks Online dashboard.
    • Select Recurring Transactions under the Lists section.
  2. Create a New Recurring Transaction
    • Click on the New button to create a new recurring transaction.
    • Choose the type of transaction you want to create, such as an invoice or sales receipt, and then click OK.
  3. Set Up the Recurring Transaction Template
    • Template Name: Enter a name for the template that will help you identify it easily.
    • Type: Select the type of recurring transaction. Options include:
      • Scheduled: For regular, predictable transactions.
      • Reminder: For transactions that need manual verification before processing.
      • Unscheduled: For transactions without a fixed schedule.
  4. Enter Transaction Details
    • Customer: Select the customer for whom the recurring transaction is being set up.
    • Interval: Specify how often the transaction should recur (e.g., monthly, weekly).
    • Start and End Dates: Set the start and end dates for the recurring transaction.
  5. Set Up Payment Method
    • Choose the payment method, such as ACH, credit card, or bank transfer. If using ACH, ensure you have the customer's bank details and authorization.
    • For credit card payments, enter the customer's credit card information.
  6. Enable Autopay (Optional)
    • If you want to enable autopay, ensure QuickBooks Payments is turned on. Customers can sign up for autopay through the invoice, and payments will process automatically for future recurring invoices.
  7. Save the Template
    • Once all the details are filled in, click Save Template to finalize the setup.

Please see the email we received today from Adam Roddy, the Senior Category Manager for Summit Behavioral Health. The attached Vendor Security Risk Assessment must be completed and filled out prior to Monday 8/26 at 3pm. I've also attached a blank copy and Kisi's copy of the initial RFP form. You are welcome to copy and adjust it and re-submit it with the Vendor Security Risk Assessment. You'll find a CCTV pricing page where I gave a ballpark MSRP cost for some of our camera partners but feel free to change this to include Rhombus's prices.


 

I will connect you via email with Adam, but as I mentioned, he is happy to answer any additional questions on a call between now and Monday.


 

Adam Roddy - Senior Category Manager

adam.roddy@summitbhc.com

+1 (423) 834-3816


 

There is a task, a "scenario bid" for cctv placement which I already did so you don't have to do it unless you want to change any of the answers. It is regarding cctv placement, my answers are below:


 

Entry/Exit Points:

 

  • Main Entry Lobby (C101): Place a camera to cover the main entry/exit point for monitoring all individuals entering or leaving the facility.
  • Stairwells (ST1.1, ST2.1): Place cameras at the entrances to these stairwells to monitor movement between floors.

 

Corridors:

 

  • Corridor (C102, C103, C105): These corridors lead to multiple critical areas and should be monitored to track the movement of staff, patients, and visitors.
  • Central Hall (C104): A camera here would provide a broad view of one of the main internal movement areas.

 

Common Areas:

 

  • Dining Room (124): Place a camera here to monitor patient and staff interactions during meal times.
  • Activity Room (127): A camera here would help monitor group activities and ensure safety.
  • Group Rooms (129, 130): Cameras in these areas should focus on entrances to monitor access but should not capture the interior due to HIPAA concerns.

 

Nurse Station (126): A camera placed here would help monitor access to sensitive areas like the medication room (126A) and nearby patient rooms.


 

Security Points:

341.content:
##########################################

  1. Email Template Creation:

import React, { useState, useRef, useEffect } from 'react';
import { Mail, Edit, Trash, Plus, X, MoreHorizontal, ChevronUp, Bold, Italic, List } from 'lucide-react';

const MAX_SUBJECT_LENGTH = 100;
const MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH = 5000;

const ConfirmationModal = ({ isOpen, onClose, onConfirm, message }) => {
 if (!isOpen) return null;

 return (
   <div className="fixed inset-0 bg-black bg-opacity-50 flex items-center justify-center z-50">
     <div className="bg-white p-6 rounded-lg shadow-lg">
       <p className="mb-4 text-lg">{message}</p>
       <div className="flex justify-end space-x-2">
         <button 
           onClick={onClose}
           className="px-4 py-2 bg-gray-200 text-gray-800 rounded hover:bg-gray-300 transition-colors"
         >
           Cancel
         </button>
         <button 
           onClick={onConfirm}
           className="px-4 py-2 bg-red-500 text-white rounded hover:bg-red-600 transition-colors"
         >
           Confirm
         </button>
       </div>
     </div>
   </div>
 );
};

const EmailTemplateManager = () => {
 const [templates, setTemplates] = useState([]);
 const [isFormActive, setIsFormActive] = useState(false);
 const [subject, setSubject] = useState('');
 const [content, setContent] = useState('');
 const [editingTemplateId, setEditingTemplateId] = useState(null);
 const [successMessage, setSuccessMessage] = useState('');
 const [errorMessage, setErrorMessage] = useState('');
 const [expandedTemplates, setExpandedTemplates] = useState({});
 const contentRef = useRef(null);
 const [isDeleteModalOpen, setIsDeleteModalOpen] = useState(false);
 const [isUnsavedModalOpen, setIsUnsavedModalOpen] = useState(false);
 const [templateToDelete, setTemplateToDelete] = useState(null);
 const [hasUnsavedChanges, setHasUnsavedChanges] = useState(false);

 useEffect(() => {
   const handleBeforeUnload = (event) => {
     if (hasUnsavedChanges) {
       event.preventDefault();
       event.returnValue = '';
     }
   };

   window.addEventListener('beforeunload', handleBeforeUnload);

   return () => {
     window.removeEventListener('beforeunload', handleBeforeUnload);
   };
 }, [hasUnsavedChanges]);

 const validateForm = () => {
   if (subject.trim().length === 0) {
     setErrorMessage('Subject cannot be empty');
     return false;
   }
   if (content.trim().length === 0) {
     setErrorMessage('Content cannot be empty');
     return false;
   }
   if (subject.trim().length > MAX_SUBJECT_LENGTH) {
     setErrorMessage(`Subject must be ${MAX_SUBJECT_LENGTH} characters or less`);
     return false;
   }
   if (content.trim().length > MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH) {
     setErrorMessage(`Content must be ${MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH} characters or less`);
     return false;
   }
   setErrorMessage('');
   return true;
 };

 const handleAddTemplate = () => {
   if (hasUnsavedChanges) {
     setIsUnsavedModalOpen(true);
   } else {
     setIsFormActive(!isFormActive);
     if (!isFormActive) {
       resetForm();
     }
   }
 };

 const handleSubmitTemplate = () => {
   if (!validateForm()) return;

   const timestamp = new Date();
   const template = {
     id: editingTemplateId || Date.now().toString(),
     subject: subject,
     content: content,
     timestamp: timestamp.toISOString()
   };
   
   if (editingTemplateId) {
     setTemplates(templates.map(t => t.id === editingTemplateId ? template : t));
   } else {
     setTemplates([template, ...templates]);
   }
   
   setSuccessMessage(editingTemplateId ? 'Template updated successfully!' : 'New template created!');
   setHasUnsavedChanges(false);
   
   setTimeout(() => {
     resetForm();
     setSuccessMessage('');
     setIsFormActive(false);
   }, 3000);
 };

 const resetForm = () => {
   setSubject('');
   setContent('');
   setEditingTemplateId(null);
   setHasUnsavedChanges(false);
   setErrorMessage('');
 };

 const handleEditTemplate = (id) => {
   if (hasUnsavedChanges) {
     setIsUnsavedModalOpen(true);
   } else {
     const template = templates.find(t => t.id === id);
     setSubject(template.subject);
     setContent(template.content);
     setEditingTemplateId(id);
     setIsFormActive(true);
   }
 };

 const handleRemoveTemplate = (id) => {
   setTemplateToDelete(id);
   setIsDeleteModalOpen(true);
 };

 const confirmDeleteTemplate = () => {
   setTemplates(templates.filter(t => t.id !== templateToDelete));
   setIsDeleteModalOpen(false);
   setTemplateToDelete(null);
   setSuccessMessage('Template deleted successfully!');
   setTimeout(() => setSuccessMessage(''), 3000);
 };

 const toggleExpandTemplate = (id) => {
   setExpandedTemplates(prev => ({...prev, [id]: !prev[id]}));
 };

 const handleContentChange = (e) => {
   setContent(e.target.innerHTML);
   setHasUnsavedChanges(true);
 };

 const handleSubjectChange = (e) => {
   setSubject(e.target.value.slice(0, MAX_SUBJECT_LENGTH));
   setHasUnsavedChanges(true);
 };

 const handleFormatText = (command) => {
   document.execCommand(command, false, null);
   contentRef.current.focus();
 };

 return (
   <div className="max-w-4xl mx-auto bg-gray-100 rounded-3xl shadow-lg p-8 transition-all duration-300 hover:shadow-xl">
     <h2 className="text-3xl font-bold mb-6 text-center text-gray-800">Email Template Manager</h2>
     
     <button 
       onClick={handleAddTemplate}
       className="w-full bg-blue-500 text-white rounded-full py-3 px-4 mb-6 transition-all duration-300 hover:bg-blue-600 hover:transform hover:-translate-y-1 flex items-center justify-center"
     >
       {isFormActive ? <X className="mr-2" /> : <Plus className="mr-2" />}
       {isFormActive ? 'Cancel' : 'Create New Template'}
     </button>
     
     {isFormActive && (
       <div className="mb-6 bg-white p-6 rounded-lg shadow-md">
         <div className="mb-4 flex items-center justify-center">
           <Mail size={40} className="text-blue-500" />
         </div>
         <div className="mb-4">
           <input
             type="text"
             value={subject}
             onChange={handleSubjectChange}
             className="w-full p-3 border border-gray-300 rounded-lg focus:outline-none focus:ring-2 focus:ring-blue-500"
             placeholder="Email Subject"
           />
           <div className="text-right text-sm text-gray-500 mt-1">
             {subject.length}/{MAX_SUBJECT_LENGTH}
           </div>
         </div>
         <div className="mb-4">

     )}
     
     {successMessage && (

     )}
     
     <div className="mt-8 space-y-6">

           <div className="flex justify-between items-center mb-3">

             <span className="text-sm text-gray-600">
               {new Date(template.timestamp).toLocaleDateString()}
             </span>
           </div>
           <div 
             className={`text-gray-700 mb-4 ${expandedTemplates[template.id] ? '' : 'max-h-20 overflow-hidden'}`}
             dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{__html: template.content}}
           />
           <div className="flex justify-between items-center">
             <button
               onClick={() => toggleExpandTemplate(template.id)}
               className="text-blue-500 hover:text-blue-700 flex items-center"

               {expandedTemplates[template.id] ? (
                 <>
                   <ChevronUp size={20} className="mr-1" />
                   Show Less
                 </>
               ) : (
                 <>
                   <MoreHorizontal size={20} className="mr-1" />
                   Show More
                 </>
               )}
             </button>
             <div className="flex space-x-2">
               <button
                 onClick={() => handleEditTemplate(template.id)}
                 className="text-blue-500 hover:text-blue-700 p-2 rounded-full hover:bg-blue-100 transition-colors duration-300"
               >
                 <Edit size={20} />
               </button>
               <button
                 onClick={() => handleRemoveTemplate(template.id)}
                 className="text-red-500 hover:text-red-700 p-2 rounded-full hover:bg-red-100 transition-colors duration-300"
               >
                 <Trash size={20} />
               </button>
             </div>
           </div>
         </div>
       ))}
     </div>

     <ConfirmationModal
       isOpen={isDeleteModalOpen}
       onClose={() => setIsDeleteModalOpen(false)}
       onConfirm={confirmDeleteTemplate}
       message="Are you sure you want to delete this template?"
     />

     <ConfirmationModal
       isOpen={isUnsavedModalOpen}
       onClose={() => setIsUnsavedModalOpen(false)}
       onConfirm={() => {
         setIsUnsavedModalOpen(false);
         resetForm();
         setIsFormActive(!isFormActive);
       }}
       message="You have unsaved changes. Are you sure you want to discard them?"
     />
   </div>
 );
};

344.content:
David, in my new IT class, we are covering a lot of material that directly relates to how we manage IT projects (i.e. how to set up UPS, best practices for client communication, safety standards, etc.). As I have been learning, I have been putting everything I learn in a big personal folder using google docs and google sites for future reference when I am more involved with projects. One of the recent sections in my class covered a bit on SOW and change orders, and I want to see if you can train me more on these topics in eCore. Lets meet and use Don's video project in eCore as practice.

#######################################################

Here's a section from one of the recent training videos I watched. I am saving a lot of the transcripts for myself:

1) Professionalism

PC technicians spend a lot of time with people. Whether in an interview, on the phone with an end user, or in a meeting with a client, you always want to leave a good impression. In this video, we're going to go over some things you can do to make your interactions more positive.

One of the best things you can do is make a good first impression. First impressions set the tone for the rest of your interactions. If you show up late, disorganized, and disheveled, you might give the impression that you're unprofessional and inconsiderate.

To make a good first impression, try to arrive a few minutes early. If you're going to be late for any reason, be sure to call ahead to see if the person would like to wait or reschedule. If you're contacted by an organization, see if you can find their dress code so you know whether you should wear formal or business casual attire. You usually find something like this on a company's website.

Be culturally sensitive and address individuals by their appropriate title. Take note of how they address themselves in any correspondence prior to your meeting. And be sure to respect people's privacy. If you're going to someone's home or office, ask them before walking in since this shows you respect them and their space. While in their space, be sure not to look at their computer screen, papers, or items on the desk.

Use proper language and avoid swearing and slang words. When possible, try to avoid industry jargon and acronyms since they might not be familiar with them. And lastly, avoid distractions. Do not accept personal phone calls or texts and don't scroll through your social media sites.

Being professional extends to identifying problems and solutions. Let's look at a few tips to consider during a service call.

First, be sure to get authorization before you make any unexpected repairs that weren't part of the original problem—especially if the extra repairs will result in an additional charge. After you've finished a repair, test the software and equipment to make sure that the issue is really fixed. You may even want to let the client test it out so they can see that the issue is really resolved.

If applicable, explain any new software or hardware that you installed, and offer additional training that might be beneficial to the client. Also, be sure to provide the client with a detailed invoice of the work you performed. Now, before you leave, make sure that the client is satisfied with your work. If the customer has any questions or concerns that are outside your expertise, help him or her contact the appropriate people, such as another technician or a manager.

As a PC technician, you're going to run into some challenging situations. Technical problems can be stressful for anyone, and many customers are going to be frustrated or anxious during your interactions.

In these stressful situations, don't be defensive or dismissive. Instead, acknowledge the customers concerns and ask open-ended questions that can help to narrow down the cause of the problem. Seek clarification. After listening to the customer, you want to restate the issue to show them that you understand. You also want to find out which outcome they're hoping for so you can explain which actions you reasonably can and cannot do.

It's up to you to set the tone, so maintain a positive attitude throughout the whole interaction. You want to project the confidence that you're up to the task. Be attentive. You don't want to do all the talking. Instead, be sure to actively listen and take notes, and don't interrupt someone while they're speaking.

You do need to set expectations. You need to clearly state which actions you're going to take and how long it'll take to complete them. Again, be sure to provide documentation on the services that were provided so that if things don't go according to plan, you have a record of your work. And be sure to follow up to answer any additional questions and to ensure satisfaction. Keep in mind that from time to time, you're going to deal with a difficult customer—someone who's rude, struggles to operate electronics, or won't accept responsibility for a problem they caused. In these situations, it's very important to remember that it's not your job to judge or belittle customers, but to help them. Keep calm and avoid arguments, and never complain about clients on social media platforms.

2) Change Management

Change is inevitable in the IT field. Whether it's updating to new equipment or changing direction mid project, you're bound to come across a lot of changes!

In this video, we're going to talk about change management. This is just the method we use to ensure that changes are implemented as smoothly and effectively as possible.

Most organizations have an official approval process for change management. A business commonly uses change order forms to document these requests.

Change order forms are different for each company, but they typically ask for the change's purpose, scope, and extent, along with a risk analysis and rollback plan in case things don't go as expected.

So, after filling out your change order form, what's next? Well, first, it must be approved by the change board. A change board might consist of one person or many people who approve changes to the project. Board members might be managers, project supervisors, and maybe even the CEO. If you were developing this project for a customer instead of for in-house use, the customer would need to approve the changes as well.

The first thing the change board will want to know is why you want to make this change at all. You'll want to explain why the change is needed and whether it'll improve a current process, save money, or add additional functionality. You might also be asked to explain how it fits within the organization's current strategic focus. The change board will also want to know the scope—what exactly the proposed change will entail from start to finish. A scope has many components, but it should always include outcomes, cost, personnel, and systems.

Some other questions you'll need to have a ready answer for are: What are your desired outcomes? What exactly do you want to change? What are the desired deliverables? How will you know when the project is complete? The board will also obviously want to know how much this is all going to cost, whether in money, time, or resources.

You'll want to consider which personnel you'll need to implement the change. Will you need developers, technicians, or administrative staff? Be sure to include the contact information for a point person who can serve as the change board's primary contact for the project, if it's approved. It's also important to explain which existing systems will be impacted. Most likely, you'll be working alongside live production systems and any changes should be carefully planned out. Will there be downtime or potential conflicts? If so, you probably want to set up a sandbox to test the proposed changes before you implement them. As you can see, if there's literally anything you think you might need for your project, you want to include it in the scope.

Before you propose a change, you also want to analyze the potential risk. Yes, even small projects come with some risk. Be sure to ask yourself, "What could go wrong if we implement these changes?" After you think through that, the next obvious questions are: How are we going to avoid these problems? How difficult will it be to backtrack if things turn out worse than expected? Is the outcome worth the risk? If it turns out that the risks outweigh the rewards, you probably want to rethink your approach.

Now, before you start anything, make sure you get written approval for your changes. Written acceptance protects you, the change board, and the customer. This ensures that all of you have a complete understanding of the proposed changes and what they could entail. You want to avoid misunderstandings that could hurt your own or your organization's reputation or that might end up causing expensive problems.

Documentation is critical to any project from start to finish! During the implementation stage, you want to be sure to document all the changes you've made along the way. Include the specific approvals you've received. Once you're done, be sure to follow your organization's end user acceptance process. This ensures that someone who's going to be using the system verifies that it's working as expected. And be sure to document this as well.

362.content:
Hi David,

Here's a simple explanation of how my new proposed progress level and status dropdown works (the bold red aspect below is the most critical). Trust me on this one. I gave it a lot of thought and this is significantly easier for everyone else using the system to understand, and it will make my tracking of my tasks and Affandy's much, much easier.

**I will come to you to show a demonstration. I used GPT and Claude to do a thorough breakdown of this functionality and any limitations it may have, and this is our best option for managing tasks.

The task management feature allows you to easily track and update the progress and status of your tasks using two dropdown menus at the top of your task list:

  1. Progress Dropdown:
    • Click on the "Progress" dropdown to see all available progress levels: All, Open, In Progress, Completed, and Closed.
    • Select a progress level to filter your tasks. For example, choosing "In Progress" will show only tasks currently being worked on.
    • The "All" option lets you view tasks at any progress level.
  2. Status Dropdown:
    • Next to the Progress dropdown, you'll find the "Status" dropdown.
    • This dropdown shows more specific states for each task, like "Awaiting Review" or "Blocked".
    • The status options change depending on the selected progress level, showing only relevant statuses.
    • If you've selected "All" in the Progress dropdown, you'll see all possible statuses here.
  3. Information Icons:
    • Next to each status in the dropdown, you'll see a small "i" (information) icon.
    • Hover your mouse over this icon to see a brief description of what that status means.
    • This helps you choose the most appropriate status for your task.
  4. Automatic Filtering:
    • If you select a specific status while the Progress is set to "All", the system will automatically update the Progress to match.
    • For example, if you choose "Blocked" status, it will set the Progress to "In Progress".
  5. Resetting Filters:
    • To see all tasks again, simply select "All" from both the Progress and Status dropdowns.

This interface makes it easy to update and filter your tasks quickly. You can get a broad overview of task progress or dive into specific statuses, all from these two simple dropdown menus. The information icons provide quick guida

When filtered to All:

 

When clicking a progress level, it will only have specific statuses available. For example, In Progress should not have the "completed" status available. We also have descriptions per status as a hover over.
 


 

Here are the rest of what shows per progress level. I asked AI to add more and critique any extra options we should have and this is the most we need before we start to have logical issues:

 

 

 



We will still have the archive functionality. Also notice QA progress level was redundant, and now a progress level of "Completed" and "In Review" will take its place

All new tasks open up to Open: & Assigned: 

 

========================

The drop down each should have these 6  statuses each 

Make sure the #1,2,3,  is next to the text,this way user knows the sequences 

 

Assignor Task Status

  1. Open: Task is created and available for assignment.
  2. Reviewed: Initial review ensures the assignee understands the task; adjustments may be in progress.
  3. QA: Task completed by the assignee - now under QA review. If QA fails, set the assignee task status to "reworking" 
  4. Completed: Task is fully done.
  5. Closed: Task is retested, completed, and closed.
  6. Awaiting Input: Suggests the task is waiting for additional information or resources.

Assignee Task Status

  1. Assigned: The task has been assigned but work has not started.
  2. In Progress: The task is currently being worked on.
  3. Awaiting Action: Implies the task is waiting for a prerequisite action.
  4. Testing: The task is in the testing phase to ensure it meets the required standards.( in Staging )
  5. Completed: The task is fully completed 
  6. Rework: Revisiting and correcting a task to meet the required standards after initial completion.

385.content:
//Button Styling:

import React, { useState, useEffect } from 'react';

const TechHomepageButton = () => {
 const [windowWidth, setWindowWidth] = useState(window.innerWidth);

 useEffect(() => {
   const handleResize = () => setWindowWidth(window.innerWidth);
   window.addEventListener('resize', handleResize);
   return () => window.removeEventListener('resize', handleResize);
 }, []);

 const getButtonStyle = () => {
   const baseStyle = {
     backgroundColor: '#EFF6FF',
     color: '#3B82F6',
     border: '1px solid #BFDBFE',
     borderRadius: '8px',
     padding: '12px 24px',
     fontSize: '18px',
     fontWeight: '500',
     cursor: 'pointer',
     transition: 'all 0.3s ease',
     boxShadow: '0 2px 4px rgba(59, 130, 246, 0.1)',
   };

   if (windowWidth <= 768) {
     return {
       ...baseStyle,
       fontSize: '16px',
       padding: '10px 20px',
     };
   }

   if (windowWidth <= 480) {
     return {
       ...baseStyle,
       fontSize: '14px',
       padding: '8px 16px',
     };
   }

   return baseStyle;
 };

 return (
   <button
     style={getButtonStyle()}
     onMouseEnter={(e) => {
       e.target.style.backgroundColor = '#DBEAFE';
       e.target.style.boxShadow = '0 4px 6px rgba(59, 130, 246, 0.2)';
     }}
     onMouseLeave={(e) => {
       e.target.style.backgroundColor = '#EFF6FF';
       e.target.style.boxShadow = '0 2px 4px rgba(59, 130, 246, 0.1)';
     }}
   >
     Tech Homepage
   </button>
 );
};

export default TechHomepageButton;

411.content:
Currently we assign task and then we have no input on its progress , issues …etc. and soly trust st assignee  to update the assignee progress.

1- We need a simple way to note each task 

2- Also see a report at the end of each day  

3- Got to be effortless 

Idea like hyper linked Tasks notes 

 

1. Automated Overdue Task Report Generation

  • Description: Automatically generate a report listing all tasks that are overdue. This report should be generated based on the "End Date" field. If the "Actually Completed" date is not set by the "End Date," the task is flagged as overdue.
  • Implementation:
    • Set up a daily or weekly cron job or script that runs at a scheduled time (e.g., end of day) to check for tasks with an "End Date" that has passed but does not have an "Actually Completed" date filled in.
    • Generate a PDF report listing these tasks, including details such as Task ID, Assignee, Start Date, End Date, Status, and the number of days overdue.
    • Distribute this report to team leads or supervisors for review and action.

2. Real-Time Alerts and Notifications

  • Description: Enhance the alert system to provide real-time notifications for overdue tasks or tasks that are approaching their "End Date."
  • Implementation:
    • Utilize the "Alert Date" field to send automatic notifications to the assignee and supervisor when a task is nearing its due date (e.g., 24 hours before the "End Date").
    • If the task status is still set to "Not Started," "In Progress," or "Awaiting Action" past the "End Date," an escalation notification is sent to both the assignee and their manager.
    • Create a notification system via email, SMS, or within the task management app to ensure all parties are aware of upcoming deadlines.

3. Task Status Audit and History Tracking

  • Description: Implement an audit trail that tracks every status change and timestamps it. This would help identify bottlenecks in the task completion process.
  • Implementation:
    • Add a "Status History" field or section to each task that logs changes in status (e.g., "Assigned" to "In Progress") along with the date and time of the change.
    • Allow this history to be exported as part of a report, which can be used to identify patterns in delays or recurring issues with specific types of tasks or assignees.
    • Use this data to evaluate the efficiency of task assignment and completion workflows.

4. Recurring Task Management and Escalation Protocols

  • Description: Create a mechanism to handle recurring tasks and ensure timely completion, even if a task is carried over multiple cycles.
  • Implementation:
    • For tasks marked as "Recurring," ensure that each instance of the task is tracked separately with its own "Start Date," "End Date," and "Actually Completed" fields.
    • Automatically flag recurring tasks that have not been completed by the "End Date" of the current cycle and send alerts or escalate to a supervisor.
    • Create a separate report for recurring tasks that details their frequency, current status, and historical completion rates.

5. Color-Coded Task Dashboard for Visual Management

  • Description: Implement a visual task dashboard that uses color-coding to quickly indicate the status of each task.
  • Implementation:
    • Use different colors to represent task statuses:
      • Green for "Completed"
      • Yellow for "In Progress"
      • Blue for "Awaiting Action (Pending Assignor)"
      • Orange for "Not Started"
      • Red for "Overdue"
    • Display this dashboard in real-time within the task management app, and provide filtering options to view tasks by assignee, department, or status.
    • Allow users to click on any task to view details, including reasons for delays or comments left by team members.

6. Weekly Progress Summary Report

  • Description: Generate a weekly summary report that lists all tasks assigned to each user, their current status, and any that are at risk of becoming overdue.
  • Implementation:
    • Set up a system that generates a summary report every week, categorizing tasks into "Completed," "In Progress," "Not Started," "Awaiting Action," "Overdue," and "Recurring."
    • Highlight tasks nearing their "End Date" and those overdue, providing a breakdown of each assignee's workload and progress.
    • Share the report with both assignees and their managers for review and further action.

7. Task Dependency and Critical Path Analysis

  • Description: Introduce a system to identify and manage task dependencies, allowing for better prioritization and understanding of which tasks are critical for project completion.
  • Implementation:
    • Add a "Dependencies" field to each task where related tasks can be linked.
    • Use this information to create a critical path analysis that visually maps out the sequence of tasks and identifies which tasks are delaying others.
    • Use this insight to focus resources on tasks that are blocking others to optimize project flow.

8. Dynamic Priority Adjustment Based on Status

  • Description: Develop an automated system that dynamically adjusts the priority of tasks based on their status and proximity to the "End Date."
  • Implementation:
    • Set up rules that increase the priority of a task as it approaches its "End Date" or if it becomes overdue.
    • Automatically update the "Priority" field from "Medium" to "High" or "Urgent" if the task's status is "Not Started" or "In Progress" with only a few days left before the due date.
    • Incorporate these adjustments into the task dashboard and reports to highlight tasks that require immediate attention.

9. Integration with Calendar Systems

  • Description: Integrate the task management system with popular calendar apps (e.g., Google Calendar, Outlook) to ensure task deadlines are visible and easily trackable.
  • Implementation:
    • Allow tasks to be synced with calendar events that show their "Start Date" and "End Date."
    • Automatically update the calendar event status based on task status changes in the task management app.
    • Use calendar notifications to alert users of upcoming deadlines and overdue tasks.

10. Feedback Loop and Continuous Improvement

  • Description: Implement a feedback loop for continuous improvement in the task management process.
  • Implementation:
    • After each task is completed, allow the assignee and assignor to provide feedback on any challenges faced, delays encountered, or improvements needed.
    • Use this feedback to refine task workflows, update task templates, and improve task assignment practices over time.

423.content:
Most CAD software's including Figma and System Surveyor have a bounding box so users cannot edit outside of the sandbox. OneSurvey needs this for floor plans, and this will also make calculations for exporting floor plans more accurate. See video and GPT breakdown below. This is very critical for us to implement and will resolve many of the issues our project managers have when it comes to sending reports to clients. 

If this is implemented successfully, I believe this may even inadvertently lead to improvements in exporting time, but we will review further in a future meeting.

Video explanation: https://www.awesomescreenshot.com/video/31673156?key=bdd7b7f284e7d5f58a0f34795fd44cfc

To address the issue of placing icons outside the background image and improve the export functionality, here are some suggestions:

1. Introduce a Bounding Box for the Floor Plan

  • Solution: Implement a bounding box or frame around the background image (floor plan) so that icons can only be placed within the boundaries of the image. You could achieve this by setting up an area within which the icons can be dragged and dropped, with snapping to prevent out-of-bounds placement.
  • Benefit: This prevents users from placing icons infinitely outside the intended floor plan, maintaining design integrity.

2. Clipping Overflowed Icons

  • Solution: If the user tries to place an icon outside the background image, automatically clip the icon to the edge of the image, ensuring no elements stray outside the bounds.
  • Benefit: Users can focus on positioning without worrying about exact boundaries, as the software will handle overflow for them.

3. Grid Overlay with Snapping

  • Solution: Add an optional grid overlay for the floor plan to help with precise icon placement. Combine this with a "snap to grid" feature so that icons naturally align with the grid and remain within the boundaries of the floor plan.
  • Benefit: Improves alignment and spacing accuracy and helps users avoid placing icons too close to the edges.

4. Auto-Scaling for PDF Export

  • Solution: Implement an auto-scaling function that fits the entire floor plan and placed icons to standard paper sizes (A4, A3, US Letter, etc.) during export. This would include logic to scale both the floor plan and icons proportionally to fit within the selected paper size.
  • Benefit: Ensures consistent export quality, regardless of the original dimensions of the floor plan.

5. Dynamic Margin Calculation

  • Solution: Calculate a dynamic margin around the floor plan, which can automatically adjust depending on the floor plan's aspect ratio and size. This would ensure that the contents are centered and have consistent spacing when exporting to a PDF.
  • Benefit: This would allow for better use of space and prevent icons or the floor plan from being too close to the edges of the PDF page.

6. Visual Export Boundary Preview

  • Solution: Add a feature where the export boundary is visually previewed on-screen, giving users a real-time view of what the PDF export will look like and how the content fits within standard page sizes.
  • Benefit: Reduces the need for trial and error when exporting, making it easy to ensure everything fits perfectly.

7. Custom Export Options

  • Solution: Provide an export settings dialog that allows users to choose paper size, orientation (portrait or landscape), and scale factors manually if they want more control over the export process.
  • Benefit: This gives advanced users more flexibility in tailoring the final output.

By implementing one or more of these features, your software should be able to handle content placement within proper boundaries while ensuring that PDF exports are clean, professional, and well-fitted to standard paper sizes.

433.content:
On hold for now:

Most of the time, when people have an issue on OneSurvey or eCore, they verbally tell us that something is broken, then it is easy to lose trackj or not have a full picture of the details. If we add an options thats easy for them to access, they could easily fill out a QUICK form that would be sent directly to us to review. if it is actually an issue, we could assign it as a task for affandy to fix. All bugs wpould be stored in the system and make it much easier to keep track of issues that need to be addressed.

I have many other things in mind for what we can add, but for the purpose of simplicity, we should start with very minimal fields, then update later.

in the beginning, I only want to include the following:

  1. Subject
  2. Description of the issue
  3. The users perception of the priority level (to be adjusted by admin before sending as task)
  4. Attachments

Once David or I receive the bug report, we can review and decide if it is an actual issue, then send it or discard it.

Let not add any complexity to it and just keep this feature very simple for now then build on top of it later, but it will be a significant improvement in keeping track regardless.

See video example: https://www.awesomescreenshot.com/video/31713102?key=ba3eb664ac8f658e80e4fd941418434c

441.content:
We are integrating the following functionalities to OneSnap starting with MOBILE ONLY first. Once mobile is completely functional, we will update the desktop interface.

  1. Switch tab to switch between different options: Gallery, Album, Archive
  2. Multiselect capability (crucial for creating galleries)
    a. A toggle button will show at the top of a gallery. After tapping, the picture tiles will enable us to multi-select them.
    b. The “Take Photo” and upload “From Device” buttons at the bottom will go away and be replaced with the following 3 icons when in multi-select mode: Create Album, Archive, Delete - more details below.

  3. Ability to Create Albums
    a. A nice slide up menu will animate into frame to allow users to create a new album or add to an existing one

    b. Once album is created or photos are added to it, automatically redirect users inside it.

  4. Albums tab

    a. The albums tab will show a tiles for all of the created albums in a OneSnap “Event” 

    b. Design: each tile will show a preview of the previous 4 photos, and show the album title, photo quantity, who uploaded, and date created.

    c. Admins can rename or delete albums, standard users can only rename.

  5. Inside the album

    a. We will show all of the photos that we added from the gallery. They will be updated in real-time, so if changes are made to the photo elsewhere, it will also change in the album.

    b. Individual picture tiles will still have an icon with 3 dots, but it will only give user the option to remove the photos from the album

    c. Towards the top, there will be another icon that we can tap to pull up a menu. This menu will show the album title that can be edited, show the creator and creation date, and give a list of options, one being to copy the public link–this public link can be seen by anyone with the link at a web url, and nothing can be edited; only the pictures from the album can be viewed.

  6. Some additional text changes, including what the delete/archive/etc. pop ups say.
  7. Updated Spinner animation where applicable.

  8. Archive tab

    a. This tab shows the archived pictures from the gallery. The UI is the same as the gallery, but individual pictures can only be unarchived or deleted. Only admins can delete.

    9. Public link to album will show a view only page of what is in the album. If the album is ever deleted, this link will no longer function.

446.content:
The following is what I designed for PHASE 1:

1 - Create a new OneSnap Album from - Mobile 

2 - archive pictures in a OneSnap Album - Mobile

3 - create public album link to a OneSnap Album (do not show archived pictures in public link or to viewers)

We are integrating the following functionalities to OneSnap starting with MOBILE ONLY first. Once mobile is completely functional, we will update the desktop interface.

  1. Switch tab to switch between different options: Gallery, Album, Archive
  2. Multiselect capability (crucial for creating galleries)
    a. A toggle button will show at the top of a gallery. After tapping, the picture tiles will enable us to multi-select them.
    b. The “Take Photo” and upload “From Device” buttons at the bottom will go away and be replaced with the following 3 icons when in multi-select mode: Create Album, Archive, Delete - more details below.
  3. Ability to Create Albums
    a. A nice slide up menu will animate into frame to allow users to create a new album or add to an existing one

b. Once album is created or photos are added to it, automatically redirect users inside it.

  1. Albums tab
  2. The albums tab will show a tiles for all of the created albums in a OneSnap “Event” 
  3. Design: each tile will show a preview of the previous 4 photos, and show the album title, photo quantity, who uploaded, and date created.
  4. Admins can rename or delete albums, standard users can only rename.
  5. Inside the album
  6. We will show all of the photos that we added from the gallery. They will be updated in real-time, so if changes are made to the photo elsewhere, it will also change in the album.
  7. Individual picture tiles will still have an icon with 3 dots, but it will only give user the option to remove the photos from the album
  8. Towards the top, there will be another icon that we can tap to pull up a menu. This menu will show the album title that can be edited, show the creator and creation date, and give a list of options, one being to copy the public link–this public link can be seen by anyone with the link at a web url, and nothing can be edited; only the pictures from the album can be viewed.
  9. Some additional text changes, including what the delete/archive/etc. pop ups say.
  10. Updated Spinner animation where applicable.
  11. Archive tab
  12. This tab shows the archived pictures from the gallery. The UI is the same as the gallery, but individual pictures can only be unarchived or deleted. Only admins can delete.

      9. Public link to album will show a view only page of what is in the album. If the album is ever deleted, this link will no longer function.

We are no longer doing the following from Priority 1 of what Sam asked as we will be updating this later after mobile is done: create a new OneSnap Album from Desktop

Section 1: Assignor's Guide

As an assignor, your role is to create, review, and finalize tasks. You control the assignor status and ensure tasks move correctly through each phase.

1. Starting a New Task

  • Initial Status:
    • Assignor Status: Open
    • Assignee Progress: Assigned
  • Reasoning:
    • When a task is created, it starts as “Open” for the assignor and “Assigned” for the assignee. This means the task is ready to be reviewed and planned.

2. Reviewing the Task

  • Next Step:
    • Change Status to: Reviewed
  • How to Review:
    1. Meet with the assignee.
    2. Discuss and agree on the task’s details, such as start date and duration.
    3. Update the task status to Reviewed once you have confirmed the details.
  • Reasoning:
    • Reviewing the task ensures that both you and the assignee are clear on what needs to be done, when it should start, and how long it will take.

3. Waiting for Task Progress

  • Allowed Assignee Progress Options:
    • Not Started: The assignee has not begun work yet.
    • In Progress: The assignee is actively working on the task.
    • Waiting Action: The assignee needs further input from you.
    • Testing: The assignee has completed the work and is testing it.
    • Completed: The task is finished and ready for your QA.
  • Reasoning:
    • These statuses reflect the work done by the assignee and help you track the task's progress.

4. Quality Assurance (QA)

  • Next Step:
    • Change Status to: QA
  • How to Perform QA:
    1. Check the task to ensure all work is completed correctly.
    2. If everything is correct, set the status to Completed.
    3. If there are issues, set the status to Rework and provide feedback to the assignee.
  • Reasoning:
    • QA ensures that the task meets the required standards before finalizing it.

5. Completing and Closing the Task

  • Final Steps:
    • Change Status to: Completed
    • Then to: Closed
  • Reasoning:
    • Marking a task as Completed confirms that it has passed QA.
    • Closed means the task is fully finished and can be archived.

Section 2: Assignee's Guide

As an assignee, your role is to progress the task through its various stages until completion. You control your progress status and update it based on the work you are doing.

1. Task Assigned

  • Initial Status:
    • Assignor Status: Open
    • Assignee Progress: Assigned
  • Reasoning:
    • This is the default starting point. You are aware of the task, but no work has started.

2. Updating Task Progress

  • Allowed Progress Updates:
  • Reasoning:
    • These updates reflect your ongoing work and help the assignor understand the task's current state.

3. Rework If Necessary

  • Rework Status:
    • If the assignor sets the task to Rework after QA, address the issues, update your progress to In Progress, and then back to Testing once corrections are made.
  • Reasoning:
    • Rework ensures that any errors are corrected before final completion.

4. Completing Your Role

  • Final Status:
    • Once testing is complete, set your status to Completed to indicate your work is done.
  • Reasoning:
    • This signals to the assignor that the task is ready for the final review and closure.

Important Notes:

  • Assignor Control: Only the assignor can change their status (e.g., from Reviewed to QA).
  • Assignee Control: Only the assignee can change their progress (e.g., from In Progress to Testing).

To automate the process of task flow , and based on task engine user guide base on 

Valid Assignor and Assignee Status Combinations with Task Duration, Start Date, and Due Date

https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1ahxRWlJpaI-QcW5nWtuKQ8EA6nKuTcxhO3clZJSx8O4/edit?gid=1786101055#gid=1786101055

 

 

 

Here's a Python program that monitors the status combinations in your task engine developed using Python and React. The program will check for invalid status combinations between the assignor and assignee. When an invalid combination is detected, it will display a pop-up message with the reason, logical solution, and the next potential action.

The program uses Python with an example of integration that can be connected to your React frontend using web sockets or API calls. For the pop-up functionality, we'll simulate it using a print statement, but in an actual implementation, this would trigger a message in your React front end.

 

 

=======================

# Import necessary modules
# Tkinter is used here for pop-up messages in the desktop environment.
# For web applications, React would use an alert, modal, or notification component.

from tkinter import Tk, messagebox

# Create a function to check the status combinations
def check_status_combination(assignor_status, assignee_progress):
   """
   This function checks the assignor status and assignee progress combination 
   and displays an error message if the combination is not allowed.
   """
   
   # Define invalid combinations with reasons and next actions
   invalid_combinations = {
       # Key is a tuple of (assignor_status, assignee_progress)
       ('Open', 'In Progress'): {
           'reason': 'Task cannot start without being reviewed; no set duration or start date.',
           'solution': 'Prevent task from moving to In Progress without being reviewed.',
           'next_action': 'Review the task and set the status to Reviewed.'
       },
       ('Open', 'Testing'): {
           'reason': 'Testing cannot occur without prior review and task progress.',
           'solution': 'Ensure the task is Reviewed and worked on before Testing.',
           'next_action': 'Review the task and update the assignee progress correctly.'
       },
       ('QA', 'Not Started'): {
           'reason': 'QA cannot occur on tasks that haven’t shown any progress.',
           'solution': 'Disallow QA status without task progressing through work phases.',
           'next_action': 'Ensure the task reaches In Progress or Testing first.'
       },
       ('Completed', 'Assigned'): {
           'reason': 'Task cannot be marked as Completed while still in the Assigned phase.',
           'solution': 'Ensure the task progresses through appropriate stages before completion.',
           'next_action': 'Move through In Progress, Testing, and QA phases before setting to Completed.'
       },
       # Add other invalid combinations as needed
   }

   # Check if the combination is invalid
   if (assignor_status, assignee_progress) in invalid_combinations:
       # Get the reason, solution, and next action for the invalid combination
       details = invalid_combinations[(assignor_status, assignee_progress)]

       # Display the pop-up message with details of the issue
       show_popup(details['reason'], details['solution'], details['next_action'])

def show_popup(reason, solution, next_action):
   """
   This function displays a pop-up message using Tkinter with the reason, solution, and next action.
   """
   # Initialize Tkinter root window
   root = Tk()
   root.withdraw()  # Hide the root window
   
   # Create a formatted message to display
   message = (
       f"This status & progress combination is not allowed. "
       f"Reason: {reason} "
       f"Solution: {solution} "
       f"Next Action: {next_action}"
   )

   # Show the pop-up message
   messagebox.showerror("Invalid Status Combination", message)

   # Close the Tkinter root window
   root.destroy()

# Example usage
# This would normally be called whenever the task status is updated in your task management system.
# Replace these values with the current status of assignor and assignee as needed.
assignor_status = 'Open'  # Example assignor status input
assignee_progress = 'In Progress'  # Example assignee progress input

# Check the combination of statuses
check_status_combination(assignor_status, assignee_progress)
